recipes.name: Simple and Amazing Peanut Butter-Chocolate Fudge

steps.text: Melt the chocolate chips with the peanut butter and maple syrup in a double boiler over medium heat, stirring continually until smooth. Pour into a dish lined with parchment paper; refrigerate 6 hours to overnight before cutting to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Simple and Amazing Peanut Butter-Chocolate Fudge
raw_recipe.description: All you need to make this fudge recipe are chocolate chips, peanut butter, and maple syrup.

review.reviewBody:
This is not a 'five-star vegan recipe' but a straight five-star recipe. 

I used:
An 8oz unsweetened (bitter) baker's chocolate cocoa bar.
Adam's (all natural) creamy p/b.
Trader Joe's Grade B Organic Maple Syrup. 

I got rave reviews from everyone that tried the fudge. I cut it smaller than the listed serving size due to the richness. It has a deeper-darker taste that is best enjoyed in small savory bites.

I don't have a double boiler yet - so I melted this in the microwave. I mixed the ingredients well in a glass bowl and microwaved for one minute then removed it and stirred alot. I repeated that once more and it became a beautiful, thick yet light, creamy hot fudge. The dominant flavour was chocolate, then peanut butter and I couldn't really tell it was maple syrup that gave it its sweetness, but I did use 100% pure Canadian Maple syrup. I also used grated dark, callebaut chocolate instead of chocolate chips. As a sauce it was delicious - hopefully I can wait the six hours to let it solidify. :) ***Update*** Once solid, it is still delicious however, I would not call it fudge. It is more like a soft chocolate square - kind of like the Moritz Icy Squares you can buy. Super yummy and super rich - so cut into small pieces. :)

This truly was easy to make. Especially since I dumped all 3 ingredients in a glass bowl and microwaved it. Recipe does not say what size pan to use. Based on the quantity that I had, I placed it in a 5 X 7.5 glass dish and got exactly 24 pieces. Next time I would like to try chunky peanut butter. Thanks for sharing!

This recipe is awesome. I made it for my sister because she is eating Vegan for Lent. She, her boyfriend, and I all loved it. Can taste the chocolate and peanut butter strongly. I used pure maple syrup and really couldn't taste it. Also I used semi-sweet baking chocolate squares instead of chips. I also added a few handfuls of cashews to add a nice surprise. I definitely will be making this again. And for those without a double boiler I used a pot about half full of water and put a stainless steel mixing bowl on top of it. That worked great.
I used corn syrup instead of maple, since most of my family doesn't like maple syrup. Worked great.

Tried last nite. Used Peter Pan creamy peanut butter, Nestles semi-sweet choc. chips & real Vermont maple syrup. Put in an 8x8 pan. Wonderful!! Can't taste the maple syrup but wonderfully creamy. May try chunky peanut butter next time. A Keeper for sure!

I have made this recipe a few times and it is always amazing! Always requests it at family gatherings. It is super quick to make and put together; I always use a 6x9 pan and the pieces come out pretty thick. Make sure that you use real maple syrup, not the Mrs. Butterworth's kind, I could see that giving an off maple flavor. This recipe has never failed for me.

This was very easy, and I loved the texture and flavor of the resulting fudge. I replaced half of the chocolate chips with unsweetened bakers chocolate, and thought the bittersweet flavor was just right.
Just delish and so easy to make 5stars

I was making it to give away... Nobody got any. I loved it. Maybe a little gooier than I'm used to, but unmistakable terrific flavor.
I put chopped walnuts in it.

I made this for Christmas & it was amazing. Smooth, soft, not too sweet, yet satisfied my sweet tooth. Perfect blend of chocolate and peanut butter and I credibly easy to make. Will most definitely make again!

Easiest dessert I have ever made. Most difficult thing: deciding which pan to put it in! Used semi sweet chocolate chips from See’s candies, MaraNatha creamy peanut butter and Grade A maple syrup. Tastes like there is plenty of sweetness to this yummy fudge!
Very easy to make, and has an amazing outcome. It tastes like something you could get at a restaurant. I always come back to this recipe!
This fudge is great! Everyone I've made it for loves it and asks for the recipe. Couldn't be easier. I followed the recipe exactly, no substitutions or changes.
So easy and delicious! Tastes just like a peanut butter cup. The fact that this is vegan is just a bonus for my vegan friends. It is great to have something so delicious from only 3 ingredients!

I really liked this. It was so easy! I made it during the same time I made hamburger helper! And it was delicious! I added a dash or two of vanilla extract in mine as well. I could see you being able to add any kind of nuts and things like that too.
I'm vegan and my brother makes this for me every year. Yum!
